#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
# counts as those scripts count and prints the rows below. The shadow classes are not
# copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each
# match exactly once (shadow-patch.py, add-patch.py), so there is no copied checker to go
# stale silently; an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts,
# and the table then says so in its #shadow row, with no counts.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #distance   the setting, the switches and the twelve targets
#   #total      distinct errors
#   #kind       by kind (errors.py): exclusion, comprises, overloading, return-type, ...
#   #class      by root cause (classify.py, distance-triage.md section 2), with its name
#   #check      a disagreement: errors.py's and table.py's totals, or sites classify.py cannot
#               find in the tree's library source
#   #unit       by the unit that printed the error first
#   #crash      each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on
#   #seconds    the run's wall time, and FortressLibrary's, the part that takes it
#   #machine    nproc, CPU model and MHz, load at start, JDK, FORTRESS_THREADS
#   #shadow     whether every shadow edit matched the tracked sources; the last row
# ../distance/compare.sh compares two tables. The run-to-run variation is 2 to 4 errors,
# in the comparisons' and Maybe's pairs and the joins of array bodies (switch-over-
# distance-flat.md section 5).
set -u

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir] [any|walk|compile]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance"
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/distance.$$}
case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac
SETTING=${3:-any}
case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_THREADS:-unset}"

# 1. the shadows, from the tracked sources (perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/make-shadows.sh's
#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" "$FH" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt"
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"

#!/bin/bash
# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
#
# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
#
#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll` and the
#                    library-order recompile (explorations/repo-internals.md, "Compile order matters") have
#                    run, and nothing since.
#   <new-worktree>   where the new worktree goes; made by `git worktree add`, reused if it already exists.
#   <branch>         the branch it checks out: an existing local branch, else origin's, else a new branch
#                    cut from <start-point>, which defaults to B; `-` makes a detached worktree at
#                    <start-point> instead. Old-against-new runs need no copy of the base: tools/old-fortress.sh
#                    runs the base build itself with a private caches folder.
#
# What it does, in order: adds the worktree; copies ProjectFortress/build, ProjectFortress/.dependencies
# and default_repository/caches from the base; renames every file of the AST caches (analyzed_cache,
# interpreter_cache, interpreter_parsed_cache) to the hash of its source's new path (NamingCzar.deCaseName,
# compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245; GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path) and rewrites the base path
# inside it; rewrites the base path in the bytecode-cache jars' SourceFile attributes (debug information
# only: jars copied unchanged also run, but their stack traces would name the base's files); and makes the
# new worktree the base's replica in its file dates too. The copies keep the base's dates (cp -a), every
# tracked file whose content is the base's takes the base file's date, and every tracked file that differs
# from B, committed or not, is stamped later than everything copied. Dates decide three things. The
# repository uses a cached entry only when it is not older than its source (repository/GraphRepository.java:244,
# :283; a changed api also makes everything that imports it stale, :600-620). Ant regenerates the AST
# nodes, the parsers and Operators.java when an input is newer than the generated file (build.xml:371-384,
# :450-467, :1335-1400); the checkout's own dates make it regenerate them, and javac then recompiles 1,077
# files. And javac recompiles a source newer than its class (build-cache-exploration.md, section 6). So the
# next `fortress compile` of a differing library source rebuilds it, and a worktree whose ProjectFortress/src
# differs from B is seeded with a warning: the copied build is B's, so the worker runs ant compileAll, which
# recompiles the differing sources (and deletes the caches, build.xml:715 and :356), and the library-order
# recompile before its first compiled run. The base's own dates must be a build's: a base built in place by
# ant, or seeded by this script.
#
# A worktree that already has ProjectFortress/build is left alone (a relaunch keeps the worker's own build);
# SEED_FORCE=1 replaces its build and caches with the base's.
#
# Prints one line per step with its time, and the seeded worktree's path last. Exits non-zero, having
# removed nothing, if the base is not built or not clean. Never touches the base or the main tree.
# Run it from anywhere; it needs bash, git, python3, realpath and bc.
set -euo pipefail

BASE_ARG=${1:?usage: seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]}
NEW_ARG=${2:?new worktree path}
BRANCH=${3:?branch}
BASE=$(realpath "$BASE_ARG")
step () { local now; now=$(date +%s.%N); printf '%-34s %5.1f s\n' "$1" "$(echo "$now - $T" | bc)"; T=$now; }
T=$(date +%s.%N); T_START=$T

# The base must be built and clean, or its caches do not describe its commit.
for f in ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/Shell.class \
         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar \
         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerLibrary.jar \
         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/CompilerSystem.jar ; do
    [ -e "$BASE/$f" ] || { echo "seed-worktree: $BASE is not built: $f is missing" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
done
if [ -n "$(git -C "$BASE" status --porcelain -- ProjectFortress Library default_repository)" ]; then
    echo "seed-worktree: $BASE has changes under ProjectFortress, Library or default_repository:" >&2
    git -C "$BASE" status --short -- ProjectFortress Library default_repository | head -5 >&2
    exit 2
fi
B=$(git -C "$BASE" rev-parse HEAD)
START=${4:-$B}

# The worktree: the same command the batch workflow's shared prefix uses, with the base commit as default.
if [ "$BRANCH" = - ]; then
    [ -d "$NEW_ARG" ] || git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q --detach "$NEW_ARG" "$START"
else
    git -C "$BASE" fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if [ ! -d "$NEW_ARG" ]; then
    git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q "$NEW_ARG" "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null \
      || git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q -b "$BRANCH" "$NEW_ARG" "$START"
fi
NEW=$(realpath "$NEW_ARG")
[ "$NEW" != "$BASE" ] || { echo "seed-worktree: the new worktree is the base" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
if [ -d "$NEW/ProjectFortress/build" ] && [ -z "${SEED_FORCE:-}" ]; then
    echo "seed-worktree: $NEW already has a build; left as it is (SEED_FORCE=1 replaces it)"

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/fortress/.claude/skills/cloud-container

# The cloud container

**container**
: Virtual machine with its own disk, on which a cloud session of Claude Code runs. It holds a clone of the branch that the session was created from.

**curator**
: Person in charge of this restoration.

**main session**
: Top-level session of a container, which the curator talks to. The agents that it launches are not main sessions.

**coordinating session**
: Main session that keeps the project's files under `explorations/coordinator/` and launches the workers.

**process stop**
: End of the session's Claude Code process, by the platform's cap, by idleness or by a VM restart. The platform starts the process again in the same session.

**VM restart**
: Restart of the container's machine under a live session.

**check-in**
: One-shot reminder, armed with `send_later`, that wakes the main session with a message at a set time.

**Stop hook**
: Command that Claude Code runs at the end of every turn of the main session.

The platform stops the session's process about every 13 hours and when the session goes idle. It can restart the VM, sometimes with the disk rolled back, and it can lose the container. Running agents survive none of these.

## Rules for every agent

- Before a long run, read the room left on the disk as `references/machine.md` says.
- If your brief lets you push, push your work as you go, as `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md` says. Only what is pushed survives a rollback of the disk or a lost container.
- After a process stop, a VM restart or a lost container, run `git status` and `git log origin/<branch>..<branch>` in each tree that you work in, before you start anything again.
- The platform's git-check Stop hook can still ask the main session to commit and push on a turn that the git-check switch misses (`references/hooks.md`). Treat its reminders as advisory. Never commit or push unready work to answer one.

## The parts

- `references/machine.md`, for every agent: the machine, timings across sessions, agents at once, the disk allowance and a full disk, the blocked hosts.
- `references/stops.md`, for every agent: the kinds of process stop and their signs, a disk rolled back, the weekly usage limit, what a stop keeps here. Its section on check-ins is for the coordinating session.
- `references/hooks.md`, for the coordinating session: the transcript backup and its blind spots, the git-check hook and how it is turned off.
- `references/container-loss.md`, for the coordinating session: re-provisioning, re-arming the backup, reading another session's transcript, recovering the work.

How a Claude Code session behaves anywhere (the Bash tool, long commands, waits and the prompt cache, interrupts, the automatic permission check) is `fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`. Running agents and resuming a run are the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`.

`references/sources.md` gives the source of each fact in these parts. Use it only to maintain this skill. Do not load it for a task.

9:## The disk allowance
10-
11:`df -h /` misleads. Its Size column is the whole disk, about 250 GB, and most of it is reserved and cannot be written. The session may use Used plus Avail, about 37 GB, and Use% is taken of that sum. Read the Avail column: it is what is left.
12-
13-- When the allowance is full, tool output fails with "no space left on device". Check Avail before a long run, and before you seed worktrees or copy builds.
14-- Temporary files that the work never deletes fill it. In this repository, they are mostly the parser's folders in `/tmp`. `fortress-repo`'s `references/build-and-caches.md` gives their sweep.
15-- When it is full, stop your own background processes (`fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`). Delete what you made and no longer need: scratch, build output, private caches, and finished worktrees whose commits are pushed.
16-- If that is not enough, commit and push, and report that this session's allowance is spent. A new session starts on a fresh machine.
17-
18-## The network
19-
20-Outbound HTTPS goes through the session's proxy, which blocks some hosts. `web.archive.org` resets the connection, and the proxy refuses `labs.oracle.com`.
21-
22-- If you need a research PDF from these hosts, name it in your report. Only the curator can upload it into the session.
23-- To read an archived page that is not a PDF, fetch it through the pure.md reader relay: `https://pure.md/https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>if_/<url>`. The `if_` after the timestamp is required.

An \apiN\ definition begins with \KWD{api}
rather than \KWD{component}.
As with components,
the identifiers associated with \apisN\ that are not included in \library\
are prefixed with the reverse of the URL of the development team.

\item
An \apiN\ does not include \KWD{export} statements.
(However, it does include \KWD{import} statements,
which name the other \apisN\ used in the \apiN\ definition.)

\item
Only declarations (not definitions!) are included in an \apiN\
definition except test and property declarations.
A method or field declaration may include the modifier \KWD{abstract}.
(Whether a declaration includes the modifier \KWD{abstract}
has a significant effect on its meaning, as discussed below).

\end{enumerate}


Import statements in APIs permit names declared in imported APIs to be used
in the importing API either qualified or unqualified,
just as in components.  Those names are \emph{not}, however,
part of the importing API,
and thus cannot be imported from that API by a component or another API.

For the sake of simplicity, every identifier reference in an \apiN\
definition must refer either to a declaration in a used \apiN\
(i.e., an \apiN\ named in an import statement,
or the Fortress core APIs, which are implicitly imported),
or to a declaration in the \apiN\ itself.
In this way, \apisN\ differ from signatures in most module systems:
they are not parametric in their external dependencies.

\section{Component and API Identity}

Formally, we introduce two functions on components,
$\imports$ and $\exports$,
that return the imported and exported \apisN\ of the component, respectively.
For any component $\comp$, %% \in \components$,
$\imports(\comp) \intersect \exports(\comp) = \emptyset$.
This restriction is required throughout to ground the semantics of
operations on components, as discussed in \secref{basicops}.

Every component
has a unique name, used for the purposes of component linking.
This name includes a user-provided identifier.
In the case of a simple component, the identifier is determined by
a component name given at
the top of the source file from which it is compiled.
A build script may keep a tally on version numbers and append them to the
first line of a component,
incrementing its tally on each compilation.
The name of a compound component is specified as an argument
to the \shellcommand{link} operation (described in \secref{basicops})
that defines it.
Component equivalence is determined nominally
to allow mutually recursive linking of components.
By programmer convention, identifiers associated with components
that are not included in \library\
begin with the reverse of the URL of the development team.
%Two components with the same name must be identical, even if they are
%contained in different fortresses.
A fortress does not allow the installation of
distinct components with the same name.
Component names are used during
\shellcommand{link} and \shellcommand{upgrade}
operations to ensure that the restrictions on
upgrades to a component are respected,
as explained in \secref{basicops}.

Every component also includes
a vendor name,
the name of the fortress it is compiled on, and
a timestamp, denoting the time of compilation.
The time of compilation is measured by the compiling fortress,
and the name of the fortress is provided by the fortress automatically.
Every timestamp issued by a fortress must be unique.
The vendor name typically remains the same throughout a significant
portion of the life of a
user account, and is best provided as a user environment variable.

Every \apiN\ has a unique name that consists of a user-provided identifier.
As with components,
\apiN\ equivalence is determined nominally.
Every \apiN\ also includes a vendor name,
the name of the fortress it is compiled on,
and a timestamp.

For convenience, a compiler can also
produce an \apiN\ directly from a project
with the same name as the component it is derived from.
Such an \apiN\ includes \emph{matching} declarations of the component.
All declarations in the component appear in the API.


A component must include, for every \apiN\ $A$ it exports,

## 2. The forks, with their defaults

**Consequential** means what the `coordinator` skill's `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", gives: it reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of yours; it touches microGPT's lines, speed or readability; it chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent; or it cannot be undone. Each fork below is marked. Each default can be undone, and none reverses a decision of yours.

### Forks the batch takes, none consequential

1. **The batch's scope: rungs I and A.** Default: as section 1 gives it. Not consequential: a choice of what is ready, by PLAN's method (the distance's decided sites first) and the planner's probe, reversible in the next batch.
2. **The arrays and decision E's diff: one rung, A.** Default: one rung (section 1). Not consequential: how the work is cut, settled by P-40's "built with the array sites' other fixes" and by the first export error, which clears only with both patches.
3. **The integer power: its own rung, I.** Default: its own rung (section 1). Not consequential: two decisions, two areas, no shared declaration, and the three patches measured applying together.
4. **The array ways as `ways.patch` has them:** the leaf `fill` and `tabulate` for 5 bodies and the `cast` for 9 (1a with 1c), the `cast` in the factory arms (2a), the `cast` of the subscript's value for `Col` and `Row` (3d). Default: as the patch. Not consequential: each is in the ways note's column of ways that need no decision (`reviews/array-sites-ways.md`, section 5), the library's own devices by P-27: a leaf redeclares a parent's method at its own type as `Array1`, `Array2` and `ImmutableArray1` redeclare `copy`, `map`, `ivmap` and `replica`, and the library's `cast` gives a factory's result its sized type, as `array1` and `array2` already do (row 685). The ways not taken, such as 1c alone and 3a's `SubArray2`, are the note's, and the rung's section names those it leaves.
5. **The api's `immutableArray` ranks 2 and 3 put in a comment** (the probe's 4d; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1500-1501`). The component has had them in a comment since the team's last commit (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2264-2280`; `a874948ac`), and the library has no `ImmutableArray2` or `ImmutableArray3`, so no program can call them. They leave the library chapter of the specification, Part IV, which is the api rendered (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27-37`). Default: as the patch; a point to report, on your review list. Not consequential: the library splits with itself, and the built side wins by the library's own standard, as for `FlatString`'s pair in climb batch 19 (`reviews/batch-19-review.md`, Part 1, split 2); the lines come back by removing the comment.
6. **A guard test of the casts at all eight element types the bound admits.** The ways note measured the casts under walk at four types and the transposed matrix (its section 6, M1), and the other four by reading. Default: A writes a walk test that asserts every cast body's value at `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR32` and `RR64`; it passes on the base and after. Not consequential: a cast that fails raises `CastError` where the base answered a value, and the guard shows none does.
7. **`MultiplicativeRing`'s `^` in the api.** The api writes `opr ^(self, other:ZZ64): T`, the component `opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral): T` with no body (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:283`, `.fss:377`). Three texts, each measured with rung A's patches beside (section 4): (a) `abstract opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral): T` alone brings a new site, 'The inherited abstract method ^ ... from the trait MultiplicativeRing[\RR64\] has no concrete implementation in the object FloatLiteral in component FortressBuiltin', since `RR64`'s api lacks the component's `opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64` (`.fss:486-487`, under the team's comment "Shouldn't need this extra declaration."); (b) the exponent alone, `AnyIntegral`, leaves the entry, which then differs, by reading, only in `abstract`; (c) `abstract` and `AnyIntegral`, with `RR64`'s api declaring the component's `opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64`: the 
8. **`QQ`'s api exponent `AnyIntegral`** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:430`, row 445's api half). Default: in rung I. Not consequential: the row's own fix, the type the component and the specification give.
9. **`QQ`'s body: the `typecase` of the probe's section 4**, the library's device for "any integer" (`exactValue`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:398-408`). Default: as probed, in `power.patch`. Not consequential: P-153's build, as the Fable judgement's section 6 gives it.
10. **`IntLiteral`'s `^` answers `IntLiteral`** (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:552-554`, `.fsi:213-214`), as the probe wrote E. Default: as probed. Not consequential: P-153's "each integer type's `^` answers its own type", applied to the numeral's type (P-76); under walk a numeral is a `ZZ32` value and reaches it once in the suite (the probe, section 1.1).
11. **Row 445's walk half, part (1): the six power natives read the exponent with `getLong`, which a `ZZ` value always refuses** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FBigNum.java:48-50`). Each native's reader is its own (`Int.java:223`, `Long.java:235`, `NN32.java:230`, `UnsignedLong.java:230`, `BigNum.java:110-116`, `IntLiteral.java:107-113`, each used by `Pow` alone). Default: in rung I: an exponent of any integer type is read, so `(1/2)^(big(3))` is `1/8`, and `XXXQQPowerExponent` is promoted and row 445 closes. Not consequential: the row's own fix, in the methods the rung edits, and it changes no value that runs today, since such a call stops walk.
12. **Row 747.** P-153 writes `fail[\ZZ32\]` in `strToInt` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4543`); the checker's gap stays for any program that writes `fail` so. Default: the row stays open with a gated expected-failure compiled test of its shape, beside `InferResultOnlyIfWithoutElse`, if the compiler's own library can state the shape; otherwise its program in its notes, and the rung says why. Not consequential: the three homes of every defect (the `fortress-repo` skill, `tests-writing.md`).
13. **Row 441.** Its claim: a negative power has no specified result, and the paths differ. After rung I, the specification gives E and walk builds it, but the compiled path's own library still answers 0, and a raw exception at 0, through `jIntExp` (row 523), until phase 4's natives. Default: a note; the row stays open with its first half fixed, as the ledger's rule for a half-fixed row says. Not consequential.
14. **The name of `DivisionByZero` in walk's natives.** Default: a constant in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/WellKnownNames.java` beside `integerOverflowException` (`:86`), read as `Int.overflow()` reads its own (`Int.java:258-261`); the probe wrote the string. Not consequential: the file's way.
15. **The team tests and demos respelled with a float base:** a `.0` on the base's numeral and nothing else: `realArith.fss:54`, `:57`; `compoundArray.fss:17-18`, `:27`, `:32`, `:33-34`; `simpleExp.fss:18-20`; `demos/BiCGSTAB.fss:211`, `demos/BiCGSTAB2.fss:198`; and `demos/npbft.fss:130`, `alpha = 10^(-6)`, which F-247's reading of the demos missed (the probe's section 1.5 lists only `npbft.fss:14`) and this record's review found by a grep of every `.fss` for an integer base at a negative exponent: P-153 names two demos, and the third is the same line in the same shape, so it goes with them. The planner's Java check: `1.0/10^k` and `Math.pow(10.0, -k)` are one double at k = 1, 2, 4 and 16, and so are the products the tests assert and print (section 4); the rung sees the respelled tests pass on the base before its edit, and where a respelled line does not keep its value or its parse there
16. **The specification's text for E:** a sentence in the method entry of `^` in `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex` (`:524-529`) and the revision box above it (`:298-320`); Appendix I's "The integer trait" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:882-1013`, its sentences at `:902-903` and `:913`) and its line in "Passages not yet revised" (`:4034`); the operators chapter's "defined in the usual way on numerals" (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:73`) left as it is, listed. Default: so. Not consequential: P-153's own words, in the revision form.
17. **No speed pass.** Neither rung changes the checker. Default: each reports the count stage's seconds and makes no speed pass. Not consequential.
18. **The second export error out, for a probe first.** The brief named its mechanical part (the ways note's 4h: `abstract` written in the api where the component's member has no body, and the plain slips) and the export check brought to `apis.tex`'s rule (4i) as a candidate. The planner's probe (section 4) found that the check names one member a trait (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:749`, `:787`, two `forall`s that stop at the first member that differs), so `Integral`'s one `abstract` line showed its next members, `one` and `numerator`; and that the same line brought a new site in `FortressBuiltin`, since `BigNum` has no `zero` that the api shows. So the extent of 4h is not known, and each line can reach another api. Default: the next batch, after a probe that runs the check to its end (4h and 4i together), on this batch's landed tree. No
19. **Row 774 out, though no longer held for you.** Your answer to ask 4 (P-154) came after the brief, which held the row for it. Its fix, walk reading an `extends` entry's `where` clause (`Constructor.boundsUnread`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Constructor.java:722-737`), changes walk's values: a list of floats loses its `<`. Nothing has measured which walk tests move. Default: the next batch, after a probe of the walk values it moves. Not consequential: it moves no site, PLAN lists it last among item 18's candidates, and a probe comes first by PLAN's method.
20. **No rung declares a checker count, a crash or a ladder move.** Default: none declared; the count and the distance reported. Not consequential.

### Points the batch lists for you, not questions

- **Team lines changed:** every integer `^` declaration of the api and the component (the team's of 2008, beside the revival's numeral overloads of 2026-10-02) and `QQ`'s body (Guy Steele's, 2008); `MultiplicativeRing`'s and `QQ`'s api powers; walk's six power natives; `strToInt`'s `fail`; the team tests `realArith`, `compoundArray` and `simpleExp` (2007) and the demos `BiCGSTAB`, `BiCGSTAB2` and `npbft` (I). The bodies of `Vector` and `Matrix` and the factory arms, wrapped in `cast`; `Col` and `Row`'s arguments; `matrix(v)`; the api's `immutableArray` ranks, `array3(v)` and the 17 operators' static parameters (A).
- **What walk does differently:** an integer raised to a negative power raises `IntegerOverflow`, or `DivisionByZero` at a base of 0, where it answered a float; `(1/2)^(big(3))` answers `1/8` where it stopped (I). No value moves by A (F-260).
- **What the checker does differently:** it types every integer power by its base; the six sites and `MultiplicativeRing`'s entry go (I); the 19 array sites and the first export error go (A).
- **What the specification says differently:** the result of an integer raised to a negative power is given (I); Part IV loses the two `immutableArray` ranks and gains `array3(v)`, `Vector`'s and `Matrix`'s `fill` and `tabulate`, and the 17 operators' shorter headers (A).

(************************************************************
* \subsection*{Reductions}
************************************************************)

trait Reduction[\L\]
    getter reverse():Reduction[\L\]
    empty(): L
    join(a: L, b: L): L
end

(** Invariants:
    join must be associative with identity empty
    unlift(lift(x)) = x
 **)
trait ActualReduction[\R,L\] extends Reduction[\L\]
    abstract empty(): L
    abstract join(a: L, b: L): L
    abstract lift(r:R): L
    abstract unlift(l:L): R
    (** If this reduction left-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    leftDistribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): Maybe[\(Reduction[\R\],Reduction[\R\])\]
    (** If this reduction right-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    rightDistribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): Maybe[\(Reduction[\R\],Reduction[\R\])\]
    (** If this reduction distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    distribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): Maybe[\(Reduction[\R\],Reduction[\R\])\]
end

trait PossibleReductionPair[\R\] extends Condition[\PossibleReductionPair[\R\]\]
    comprises { NoReductionPair[\R\], SomeReductionPair[\R\] }
end

(************************************************************
* Reductions
************************************************************)

trait Reduction[\L\]
    getter reverse():Reduction[\L\] = ReversedReduction[\L\](self)
    empty(): L
    join(a: L, b: L): L
end

object ReversedReduction[\R\](r:Reduction[\R\]) extends Reduction[\R\]
  getter reverse():Reduction[\R\] = r
  getter asString():String = "ReversedReduction(" || r.asString || ")"
  empty():R = r.empty()
  join(x:R,y:R):R = r.join(y,x)
end

(** Invariants:
    join must be associative with identity empty
    unlift(lift(x)) = x
 **)
trait ActualReduction[\R,L\] extends Reduction[\L\]
    lift(r: R): L
    unlift(l:L): R
    (** If this reduction left-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    leftDistribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\] =
        distribute(r)
    (** If this reduction right-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    rightDistribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\] =
        distribute(r)
    (** If this reduction distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    distribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\] =
        NoReductionPair[\K\]
end

trait PossibleReductionPair[\R\] extends Condition[\PossibleReductionPair[\R\]\]
    comprises { NoReductionPair[\R\], SomeReductionPair[\R\] }
end

object NoReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean = false
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G = e()
end

    getter isAnyBounded(): Boolean = self.left.holds OR self.right.holds
    truncL(l:I): BoundedRange[\I\]

    opr INTERSECTION(self, other: Range[\I\]): Range[\I\]

        It is assumed that %self% describes the bounds of some object;
        %narrowToRange% yields the subset of this index space that lie
        in %other%.  Unlike %INTERSECTION%, %narrowToRange% signals an
        error if the result is empty, neither argument is, and:
          * The minimum bound of %other% is less than the minimum
            bound of %self%.
          * The maximum bound of %other% is greater than the maximum
            bound of %self%.

        In previous versions of Fortress ranges we did more vigorous
        checking, but this proved to be merely annoying (preventing or
        requiring special kludges for eg. indexing with a lower bound
        past the end of a collection to obtain the empty collection).

Climb batch 7R, rung J (the ranges decision, POSITIONS 2026-09-27, the
numerics plans, decision 1; rows 358 and 452). RangeInternals and the #, :
and :: operator block of FortressLibrary declare no integer type parameter,
since a numeral never converts to a type named by a type parameter; every
ZZ32 range keeps its values, a range over ZZ64, NN32, NN64 or ZZ now stops

declares; in the one-library world it now asks whether a trait-typed
guard's type has Contains among its ancestors, so ExtentScalarRange no

    another indexed generator internally.  By default, this in turn
    is defined in terms of %indexValuePairs()%.  Thus, it is only
    necessary to define either %indexValuePairs()% or %indices()%.

    getter size(): ZZ32

A constructor declaration has a (possibly empty) parenthesized list of
value parameters.  Each value parameter of a constructor declaration
may be preceded by the special modifier \KWD{transient} or by a
sequence of field modifiers.  A value parameter preceded by the
modifier \KWD{transient} does not correspond to a field in an
instantiation of the object: \KWD{transient} parameters are not in
scope in the object's method declarations, but are in scope when
the initial-value expressions of the fields
are evaluated during object creation.

For example, the following leaf object extending trait \TYP{Tree}:
\input{\home/basic/examples/Object.Decl.Leaf.tex}
has no fields and two methods.



Here is an example of a \TYP{Cons} object constructor extending

\input{\home/basic/examples/Object.Decl.Cons.tex}
Note that this declaration introduces the ``factory'' function
%Cons[\T\](first:T,rest:List[\T\]):Cons[\T\]
\EXP{\TYP{Cons}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket(\VAR{first}\COLONOP{}T,\VAR{rest}\COLONOP\TYP{List}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket)\COLONOP\TYP{Cons}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket}
which is used in the body of the object declaration to define the \VAR{cons}
that fields were always ``private.'' -- Scott}
Fields are variables local to an object.
They must not be referred to outside their enclosing object declarations.
Each field is either a non-transient value parameter of a constructor
declaration, or it is explicitly defined by a field declaration within the body of a constructor
declaration, a singleton declaration, or an object expression
(described in \secref{object-expr}).
A field declaration in an object declaration is syntactically identical to
a top-level variable declaration (described in \secref{top-var-decls}),
with the same meanings attached to the form of variable declarations.
Additional modifiers apply to fields, as described in \secref{abstract-fields}.  Unlike with an abstract field in a trait declaration, an object declaration may declare a \KWD{hidden} field which is not \KWD{settable}.

Each field declaration includes an \emph{initial-value} expression,
which specifies the initial value of that field.
Field initialization occurs in textual program order:
evaluation of each initial-value expression
must complete before evaluation of the next initial-value expression,
and all previous field names
(and the parameters of the constructor,
in a constructor declaration)
are in scope when evaluating an initial-value expression
(see~\secref{scope}).
All fields of an object are initialized
before that object is made available for subsequent computation;
thus,
it is illegal to invoke methods on
an object being initialized:
\KWD{self} is \emph{not} implicitly declared by a field declaration.

# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <last-landed-table|""> <this-table>
#
# Prints one verdict line, then every #kind and #class row whose count moved, with the
# change, and every #crash row that went or came. It is REPORTED and never red: it always
# exits 0, whatever moved, a stale shadow and a run that produced no table included (Pavol,
# answer 11, POSITIONS.md 2026-09-26: a report-only stage, whose job is driving the distance
# down). The verdicts:
#   DISTANCE DOWN|UP|SAME   <last> -> <now>
#   DISTANCE FIRST          no landed table to compare with
#   DISTANCE NO TABLE       this run produced no count, with the table's own reason
#   SETTING CHANGED         the two tables ran different settings: the counts are not like for like
#   SHADOW STALE            a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources
# A move of 2 to 4 errors in the components' type errors or in which pair of LEXICO, SQCAP or
# INVERSE declarations an overloading error names is the checker's run-to-run variation
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md section 5), not a change; a crash row whose line numbers
# moved because a rung edited above it prints as one gone and one new.
set -u

field () { awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '$1 == t { sub("^[^\t]*\t", ""); print; exit }' "$2" ; }

now=$(field '#total' "$NEW")
sh=$(field '#shadow' "$NEW")
case "$sh" in STALE*) echo "SHADOW STALE   ${sh#STALE: }" ;; esac
case "$now" in

# The follow-on of the 4h patch: each implementing trait's api shows the concrete members its component defines,
# where an abstract line of 4h reaches an object of another component. Applied after make-4h.py.
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
L = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
def block(header):
    i = [k for k, l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith(header)]
    assert len(i) == 1, header
    j = i[0]
    while L[j] != 'end': j += 1
    return i[0], j
def insert_after(lo, hi, anchor, new):
    k = [n for n in range(lo, hi) if L[n] == anchor]
    assert len(k) == 1, (anchor, k)
    L[k[0]+1:k[0]+1] = new
def insert_before(lo, hi, anchor, new):
    k = [n for n in range(lo, hi) if L[n] == anchor]
    assert len(k) == 1, (anchor, k)
    L[k[0]:k[0]] = new
# bottom-up, so that each block's indices hold
lo, hi = block('trait OpenRange[\\I\\] extends PartialRange')
insert_after(lo, hi, '    opr IN(n: I, self): Boolean',
             ['    shiftLeft(amount: I): OpenRange[\\I\\]', '    shiftRight(amount: I): OpenRange[\\I\\]'])
lo, hi = block('trait ZZ extends { AnyIntegral, Integral[\\ZZ\\] }')
insert_after(lo, hi, '    opr /(self,other:ZZ):QQ',
             ['    opr %s(self, b: ZZ): ZZ' % o for o in 'DIV REM MOD GCD LCM CHOOSE BITAND BITOR BITXOR'.split()] +
             ['    opr LSHIFT(self, b:AnyIntegral): ZZ', '    opr RSHIFT(self, b:AnyIntegral): ZZ', '    opr BITNOT(self): ZZ'])
insert_before(lo, hi, '    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):ZZ', ['    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):ZZ'])
insert_after(lo, hi, '    coerce(x: IntLiteral)', ['    getter zero(): ZZ', '    getter one(): ZZ'])
for t in ('ZZ64', 'ZZ32'):
    lo, hi = block('trait %s extends { AnyIntegral, Integral[\\%s\\] }' % (t, t))
    insert_before(lo, hi, '    opr ^(self, b:IntLiteral):%s' % t, ['    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):%s' % t])
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(L))
print('edited', p)
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# mg-run.sh <work-dir> <label> [threads] [full]: the two microGPT checks under walk, each from an empty
# private cache (FORTRESS_CACHES) in a fresh folder under <work-dir> (old runs' folders stay; clear them by hand), each run from its own directory as its header says, both at once,
# with bin/fortress's own JVM (JAVA_FLAGS -Xmx4g -Xss64m) and FORTRESS_THREADS=<threads> (default 1).
# By default the quick pair, MicroGptFlatQuick and MicroGptAplQuick: two forward-and-backward passes each, 7 checks against the goldens,
# timeout 600 s.  With the word full in any position, the full pair, MicroGptFlatCheck and MicroGptAplCheck: 40 checks each, timeout 5400 s.
# Output to <work-dir>/<name>.txt, headed by the machine line (machine.sh) and ended by rc=.
set -u
PROGS="explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlatQuick.fss explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptAplQuick.fss"; LIMIT=600; A=()
for a in "$@"; do
  if [ "$a" = full ]; then PROGS="explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlatCheck.fss explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptAplCheck.fss"; LIMIT=5400
  else A+=("$a"); fi
done
set -- "${A[@]}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."                               # $FORTRESS_HOME
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH="/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH" FORTRESS_HOME="$(pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=${3:-1}
W=$(mkdir -p "${1:?usage}" && cd "$1" && pwd)
L=${2:?usage}
for f in $PROGS; do
  (
    t=$(basename "$f" .fss)
    R=$(mktemp -d "$W/run-$t-XXXX"); C="$R/caches"; T="$R/tmp"; mkdir -p "$C" "$T"   # a fresh folder per run; nothing is deleted
    printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$C/global.map"
    {
      bash explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/machine.sh "$L $t"
      start=$(date +%s)
      ( cd "$(dirname "$f")" && FORTRESS_CACHES="$C" JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$T" \
          timeout -k 10 $LIMIT "$FORTRESS_HOME/bin/fortress" "$(basename "$f")" < /dev/null )
      echo "rc=$? secs=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))"
    } > "$W/$t.txt" 2>&1
  ) &
done
wait

content.content:
If your edit is in one of these, your own tests are its only check. Say so in your report.

## One test, or a few

Each script and `fortress junit` below ends with the verdict of JUnit's text runner: `OK (n tests)`, or `FAILURES!!!` with the counts. Read the verdict there: the exit code is 0 whatever the verdict.

### Interpreter tests

Run interpreter tests (`ProjectFortress/tests/`) from the tree's root, after you set up the call:

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh <tree>/tmp/h1 \
        ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss [ProjectFortress/tests/X.test] [more files ...]

- It runs `SystemJUTest` with testSystem's JVM settings, at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, on a folder that holds only the files that you name.
- It keeps its cache in the folder `<scratch-dir>.cache`. It starts from that cache while the build and the library sources are those that filled it. Otherwise, or with `COLD_CACHE=1`, it starts empty. Its first line says `cache filled` or `cache empty`.
- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing. After you edit Java, Scala or a parser grammar, run `ant compileAll` first. If your tree has no build, seed it or build it as `worktrees.md` says.
- Give it a scratch directory that holds nothing else. The script deletes the directory when it starts and when it ends.
- If a test has an `X.test` file (its keys for a refusal at load), name it beside its `X.fss`.
- It takes 15 to 25 s with an empty cache, mostly to analyse the library, and about 4 s with a filled one. Name several files in one call to run them in one JVM.
- It shows the output of passing tests too, and removes the Java stack frames.

# The export check of FortressLibrary, run to its end

## In short

- **The 43 entries hide 115 differences, and 4 more.** The stock check names, of each trait, only the first member that differs, and stops at a trait whose api lists more members than its component. A shadow that compares every member, by name as well as by header, finds 115 differences that the stock rules report one trait at a time, in the 43 traits and objects. It also finds 4 more that the stock check accepts only because it matches a trait's members without their names. Section 2 lists them all.
- **Sorted (section 3):**

  | What clears it | Differences |
  |---|---|
  | 4h: `abstract` written in the api where the component's member has no body | 56 |
  | 4h: the api declares a bodyless member of the component that it lacks | 3 |
  | 4h: plain slips | 7 |
  | 4i: the check brought to `apis.tex` | 8 |
  | Neither, and no decision by my reading | 17 |
  | A decision | 6 |
  | Waits elsewhere: `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` (P-90), `String` (P-155) | 5 + 13 |
  | **Total** | **115** |

  Two of 4h's 56, `QQ`'s `numerator` and `denominator`, also need a fix of the check: it compares their `self` types with the api's and the component's sides swapped (section 6, defect 3). The 4 differences that the stock check accepts by the name gap go 1 to neither, 2 to decisions and 1 to String.
- **The 4h patch: the distance goes from 5 to 28** (section 4). The export error stays, its entries 43 → 20. The two `BIG MIN` sites and the two OT sites stay. 23 new errors come, all `abstract-method`: 17 in `FortressBuiltin` (`BigNum` 15, `Int` 1, `Long` 1) and 6 in `RangeInternals` (the three open ranges, 2 each). Each one comes from an `abstract` line in `Integral` or `Range`, where the api of the trait that implements the member does not show the component's concrete member. With 19 more api lines that show those members, the 23 go and nothing else comes: the distance is 5 again, with 20 entries.
- **4i after 4h** clears 10 more differences (8, and String's 2): 51 → 41, entries 20 → 15. What then remains is the 25 differences of neither and of a decision, and the 16 of `Maybe` and `String` that are left after 4h and 4i.
- **Walk:** microGPT's quick pair passes on the patch, 7 of 7 each, and so do nine walk tests of the patched traits (section 4.4).
- **Found on the way** (section 6): the check matches members without their names. Its field comparison ignores names and modifiers, through a Scala newline. Its component-to-api half swaps its arguments into a one-sided self-type comparison. And the distance stage prints `#total 0` for a library that does not parse.

## 1. How it was measured

### The shadow

`export-check-shadow.patch` edits `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala`, in a copy compiled into a scratch folder that comes ahead of the build on the class path. The stock check, which is the team's (`^5a68404fd`, the history's boundary), stops at two places:

- `equalListMembers` returns "missing members" when the api's trait lists more members than the component's (`ExportChecker.scala:768-769`), and else ends in `inAPI.forall(handleOne)` (`:787`).
- `allAbstractsMadePublic` ends in `inComp.forall` (`:749`).

The shadow makes both of them map over every member, and it keeps the stock verdict. Beside the verdict, it prints one `#XDIFF` line for each difference: the trait, the kind, the member, the api's and the component's spans, and the two headers. For every member it also looks up the members of the same name on the other side, which the stock check never does (section 6, defect 1).

Its kinds:

- **Header clauses:** `header-extends`, `header-excludes` and the rest.
- **The api's members:** `api-member-missing` (no member of the name in the component), `abstract-component-only`, `abstract-api-only`, `api-member-differs` (with the differing parts: static parameters, modifiers, parameter types, return type), and `api-matched-by-other-name` (the stock check accepts the member through a member of another name).
- **The component's abstract members:** `comp-abstract-absent`, `pair:abstract-component-only` (the other half of an api-side pair), `comp-abstract-differs` and `comp-abstract-matched-by-other-name`.

With `PROBE_EXPORT_4I` set in the environment, the shadow applies 4i (section 3.2).

A difference is counted once:

- one for each api member with no satisfying component member by the stock rules, where a pair that both halves of the check report counts once;
- one for each component abstract member that the api does not declare;
- one for each header clause.

The stock "missing members" verdict is no difference of its own, since the shadow lists its members one by one. A member that the stock check accepts by another member's name is counted apart, as "accepted by the name gap", unless the other half of the check already counts the pair.

The commands, from the tree's root after the skill's setup lines:

    F=ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala ; S=$PWD/tmp/shadow
    mkdir -p $S/src $S/classes && cp $F $S/src/ExportChecker.scala
    patch $S/src/ExportChecker.scala < explorations/perf-probes/export-check-full/export-check-shadow.patch
    CP=$(bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
    java -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -classpath "$CP" -d $S/classes -encoding UTF-8 $S/src/ExportChecker.scala
    sed 's#-cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:#-cp "${XCP:+$XCP:}$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:#' \
        explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh > tmp/run-shadow.sh && chmod +x tmp/run-shadow.sh
    XCP=$S/classes tmp/run-shadow.sh tmp/d/distance.txt tmp/d          # PROBE_EXPORT_4I=1 before it for 4i
    grep '^#XDIFF' tmp/d/run.txt | cut -f4 | sort | uniq -c            # the lines by kind

On the landed library this prints 190 lines. 33 are `abstract-component-only`, 58 `pair:abstract-component-only`, 32 `api-matched-by-other-name`, 24 `api-member-differs`, 16 `api-member-missing`, 10 `member-count`, 7 `header-extends`, and 3 each `abstract-api-only`, `comp-abstract-absent` and `comp-abstract-matched-by-other-name`; 1 is `header-excludes`. They make the 115 differences, and the 4 accepted by the name gap.

### The runs

Each run is one distance stage, about 140 s. The machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, 2100 MHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`. The load at start was 0.5 to 5.1, with other agents beside.

| Run | Library | Checker | `#total` | Export entries | Shadow's differences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gate, climb batch 20 (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-20/gate/distance.txt`) | landed | stock | 5 | 43 | |
| S1 | landed | shadow | 5 | 43 | 115, and 4 accepted by the name gap |
| A | `library-4h.patch` | stock | **28** | 20 | |
| S2 | `library-4h.patch` | shadow | 28 | 20 | 51 (after 4h: 49, and `QQ`'s 2, section 6, defect 3) |
| S3 | `library-4h.patch` | shadow with 4i | 28 | 15 | 41 |
| B | `library-4h.patch` and the 19 follow-on lines (section 4.3) | stock | **5** | 20 | |

The shadow keeps the stock verdict, so S1's table equals the gate's: `#total 5`, `X1 1`, `BR 2`, `OT 2`. S1 ran twice, with the shadow before and after its 4i switch was added, and its `#XDIFF` lines were the same both times (`cmp` of the two extracts). Every table ends `#crash none` and `#shadow every shadow edit matched the tracked sources`. The stock tables compare with the gate's per-site list by `explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/compare-sites.py`.

## 2. Every difference

The stock check's message on the landed tree names these 43 traits and objects (`compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, row 1):

- Equality, Comparison, EqualTo, StandardMin, StandardMax, Number, RR64, QQ, Integral;
- Condition, AnyMaybe, Maybe, Just, Nothing, AnyUniqueItem;
- Indexed1, Indexed2, Indexed3, Indexed, ZeroIndexed, DelegatedIndexed;
- ReadableArray, ReadableArray1, ImmutableArray1, Array1, Array2, Array3;
- Reduction, ActualReduction, ReductionPair, BigReduction, Comprehension;
- FilterGenerator, Range, OpenRange, RangeWithExtent, BoundedRange, RangeWithLeft, RangeWithRight, FullRange;
- String, Generator2, RelationalPredicateCondition.

Every difference in them, in the api's order. Lines are `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` (fsi) and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` (fss) at the base. "No body" means that the component's member is abstract.

| Trait or object | What differs | n | Members |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equality | `abstract` in the api, a body in the component | 1 | `=` (fsi:74, fss:101) |
| Comparison | a bodyless member of the component that the api lacks | 1 | `getter asString(): String` (fss:135) |
| EqualTo | the api's `<(self, other:LessThan)`, the component's `<(self, other:GreaterThan)` | 1 | `<` (fsi:163, fss:210) |
| StandardMin, StandardMax | no body in the component, no `abstract` in the api | 2 | `MIN` (fsi:194), `MAX` (fsi:206) |
| Number | the same | 1 | `asFloat` (fsi:289) |

## 6. Defects found on the way

1. **The export check matches a trait's members without their names.**
   - `equalFnHeaders` binds the header's name to `_` (`ExportChecker.scala:600`, `SFnHeader(sparamsL, modsL, _, …)`), and `equalMember` compares nothing else.
   - So an api member is satisfied by any component member with its header, and a component abstract member is "declared in the API" by any api member with its header.
   - On this library that hides 4 differences (section 2) and lets 32 pairs pass on the api's half. `String`'s `||(self, b:String)` passes through `|||` (fsi:2496, fss:4417), and `Integral`'s `+` through `MINNUM`.
   - The text asks for "a definition d' with the same name as d" (`apis.tex:250-251`). No ledger row holds it (`ledger-find:ExportChecker`, `ledger-find:export check`: rows 637, 737, 768, 769, 782, 584, 603, 604, 784 are other gaps).
   - Shown by the shadow's `api-matched-by-other-name` lines; no test.
2. **Its field comparison ignores names and modifiers.** `equalLValue` (`ExportChecker.scala:812-821`) writes `equalIds(nameL, nameR) && modsL.equals(modsR)` on one line and the type `match` on the next. Scala reads a newline before `(` as the end of a statement, so the first line is discarded and only the types are compared.
   - A ten-line Scala program of the same shape, compiled with the tree's scalac 2.13.18, prints 'names compared' and 'different names, same type: true'.
   - No difference of this library trips it (no field line among the shadow's), so it hides nothing here.
   - No ledger row.
3. **Its component-to-api half compares with the arguments swapped, against a one-sided self-type rule.**
   - `allAbstractsMadePublic` calls `equalMember(d, r)` with the component's member `d` where `equalMember` takes the api's (`:752`, `:791`).
   - `equalTypes` accepts two self types when the left one's list is empty (`:485-488`, under the team's note that `comprises {...}` and a plain self type share that encoding).
   - `QQ`'s api writes `comprises { ... }` and its component `comprises { Ratio }` (fsi:399, fss at `trait QQ`). So the component's `abstract numerator(self:(QQ & {Ratio}))` never matches the api's `abstract numerator(self:QQ)`, while the api's half, which calls it the other way round, matches it (run S2's `comp-abstract-differs` lines, with no differing part).

# The export check of FortressLibrary, run to its end

## In short

- **The 43 entries hide 115 differences, and 4 more.** The stock check names, of each trait, only the first member that differs, and stops at a trait whose api lists more members than its component. A shadow that compares every member, by name as well as by header, finds 115 differences that the stock rules report one trait at a time, in the 43 traits and objects. It also finds 4 more that the stock check accepts only because it matches a trait's members without their names. Section 2 lists them all.
- **Sorted (section 3):**

  | What clears it | Differences |
  |---|---|
  | 4h: `abstract` written in the api where the component's member has no body | 56 |
  | 4h: the api declares a bodyless member of the component that it lacks | 3 |
  | 4h: plain slips | 7 |

  | A decision | 6 |

  Two of 4h's 56, `QQ`'s `numerator` and `denominator`, also need a fix of the check: it compares their `self` types with the api's and the component's sides swapped (section 6, defect 3). The 4 differences that the stock check accepts by the name gap go 1 to neither, 2 to decisions and 1 to String.

The two `BIG MIN` sites and the two OT sites stay. 23 new errors come, all `abstract-method`: 17 in `FortressBuiltin` (`BigNum` 15, `Int` 1, `Long` 1) and 6 in `RangeInternals` (the three open ranges, 2 each). With 19 more api lines that show those members, the 23 go and nothing else comes: the distance is 5 again, with 20 entries.
- **4i after 4h** clears 10 more differences (8, and String's 2): 51 → 41, entries 20 → 15. What then remains is the 25 differences of neither and of a decision, and the 16 of `Maybe` and `String` that are left after 4h and 4i.
- **Walk:** microGPT's quick pair passes on the patch, 7 of 7 each, and so do nine walk tests of the patched traits (section 4.4).
- **Found on the way** (section 6): the check matches members without their names. Its field comparison ignores names and modifiers, through a Scala newline. Its component-to-api half swaps its arguments into a one-sided self-type comparison. And the distance stage prints `#total 0` for a library that does not parse.

## 1. How it was measured

### The shadow

`export-check-shadow.patch` edits `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala`, in a copy compiled into a scratch folder that comes ahead of the build on the class path. The stock check, which is the team's (`^5a68404fd`, the history's boundary), stops at two places:

- `equalListMembers` returns "missing members" when the api's trait lists more members than the component's (`ExportChecker.scala:768-769`), and else ends in `inAPI.forall(handleOne)` (`:787`).
- `allAbstractsMadePublic` ends in `inComp.forall` (`:749`).

The shadow makes both of them map over every member, and it keeps the stock verdict. Beside the verdict, it prints one `#XDIFF` line for each difference: the trait, the kind, the member, the api's and the component's spans, and the two headers. For every member it also looks up the members of the same name on the other side, which the stock check never does (section 6, defect 1).

Its kinds:

- **Header clauses:** `header-extends`, `header-excludes` and the rest.
- **The api's members:** `api-member-missing` (no member of the name in the component), `abstract-component-only`, `abstract-api-only`, `api-member-differs` (with the differing parts: static parameters, modifiers, parameter types, return type), and `api-matched-by-other-name` (the stock check accepts the member through a member of another name).
- **The component's abstract members:** `comp-abstract-absent`, `pair:abstract-component-only` (the other half of an api-side pair), `comp-abstract-differs` and `comp-abstract-matched-by-other-name`.

With `PROBE_EXPORT_4I` set in the environment, the shadow applies 4i (section 3.2).

A difference is counted once:

- one for each api member with no satisfying component member by the stock rules, where a pair that both halves of the check report counts once;
- one for each component abstract member that the api does not declare;
- one for each header clause.

The stock "missing members" verdict is no difference of its own, since the shadow lists its members one by one. A member that the stock check accepts by another member's name is counted apart, as "accepted by the name gap", unless the other half of the check already counts the pair.

The commands, from the tree's root after the skill's setup lines:

    F=ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala ; S=$PWD/tmp/shadow
    mkdir -p $S/src $S/classes && cp $F $S/src/ExportChecker.scala
    patch $S/src/ExportChecker.scala < explorations/perf-probes/export-check-full/export-check-shadow.patch
    CP=$(bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
    java -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -classpath "$CP" -d $S/classes -encoding UTF-8 $S/src/ExportChecker.scala
    sed 's#-cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:#-cp "${XCP:+$XCP:}$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:#' \
        explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh > tmp/run-shadow.sh && chmod +x tmp/run-shadow.sh

    grep '^#XDIFF' tmp/d/run.txt | cut -f4 | sort | uniq -c            # the lines by kind

### 3.2 4i, 8 (and String's 2)

These are `Equality`'s `=`, `Indexed`'s `size` and `|self|`, `ActualReduction`'s `empty` and `join`, `AnyMaybe`'s `holds`, `Range`'s `isEmpty` and `ReadableArray`'s `opr[_:TrivialOpenRange]`, with `String`'s `splitWithOffsets` and `split`. Each is an api member written `abstract`, whose component member has a body, or a different header, or does not exist.

How the shadow applies 4i (`PROBE_EXPORT_4I`):

- An api member written `abstract` needs no satisfying declaration (`apis.tex:249-256`: "other than the methods or fields declared abstract in d"). In the api-to-component direction this also covers 4i's first rule, a concrete member satisfying an abstract one.
- The "missing members" count counts the api's non-abstract members only. Without this, the second rule cannot clear the entries of `ActualReduction`, `AnyMaybe`, `Range` and `ReadableArray`, whose api lists more members than the component (`ExportChecker.scala:768`).

The component-to-api half is unchanged. Run S3 on the 4h tree: 51 → 41 differences, entries 20 → 15. `Equality`, `Indexed`, `ReadableArray`, `Range` and `AnyMaybe` leave the message.

### 3.3 Neither 4h nor 4i, and no decision by my reading: 17

- **An object field's getter, 4** (`BigReduction`'s `reduction`; `Comprehension`'s `reduction`, `body`, `unwrap`). These are the team's lines on both sides (`^5a68404fd`).
  - The component's value parameters are fields, and a field is local to its object (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:268-271`), but it carries a getter. The api writes the getters and names the parameters otherwise. The check reads neither the getters of the component's fields nor the parameters' names (`equalParams` compares types and modifiers only).
  - Two ways. (a) A check rule beyond 4i: a component object's value parameter satisfies an api getter of its name and type. (b) The api names the parameters as the component does, and drops the getters that restate them.
- **An api form that the component never defined, 4** (`opr[_:OpenRange[\ZZ32\]]` of `ImmutableArray1`, `Array1`, `Array2` and `Array3`). The team's api had them and its component did not, at `a874948ac`. Fork 5's way, the api lines out as climb batch 20 did for `immutableArray`'s ranks, applies. It removes four operators from Part IV, so it is a point to report, as fork 5 was (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-20.md`, fork 5).
- **A result type that the api cannot name, 4** (`Array2`'s and `Array3`'s `bounds` and `zeroIndices`). The component answers `RangeInternals.CompactFullRange2D` (`3D`). The team's component did too, with static arguments (`a874948ac`; `3be1fecd7` dropped them). The api imports nothing from `RangeInternals`. `CompactFullRange2D` extends `CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32, ZZ32)\]` (`Library/RangeInternals.fsi:520-521`). So the component can declare the api's type, if none of its bodies needs the narrower one. Not measured.
- **The api's older signature, 3** (`ActualReduction`'s `leftDistribute`, `rightDistribute`, `distribute`). Only the component's form, `[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\]`, is built and used: by the reductions (fss:3435-3451) and by `Library/Generator2.fss:73-79`. The api declares `PossibleReductionPair` itself (fsi:1902). The way is the api taking the component's three headers. It changes Part IV (a point to report).
- **`DelegatedIndexed`, 2.**
  - Its api restates `getter size(): ZZ32`, which the component's trait inherits from `Indexed`'s body (fss:1967). The way is the line out of the api, or a check rule that counts inherited bodies. The line out makes `size` abstract again for `DelegatedIndexed`'s extenders in other components (`FlatString`, `Library/FlatString.fss:34-35`, defines it), so it needs a run.
  - Its `generator` answers `Indexed[\E,I\]` in the component and `Generator[\E\]` in the api. `FlatString` overrides it at `Generator[\Char\]` (`FlatString.fss:45`) against the api's type, so the api's is the one that other components rely on. The way is the component widened to the api's type: its bodies call only `Generator` methods on it (fss:2092-2105).
- And of the 4 accepted by the name gap: `TotalComparison`'s `=`, by the api writing the component's two forms.

### 3.4 A decision, 6

- **`RR64`'s rounding, 3:** `|\self/|` and `|/self\|` answer `ZZ64` in the api and `ZZ` in the component, and `truncate` answers `ZZ64` in the api and `RR64` in the component (fsi:377-380, fss:498-501, both the team's). This is a contract of the number types that no decision on record names (my reading). Beside it, accepted by the name gap: `^(self, b:RR64)` in the api and `^(self, b:Number)` in the component, next to P-153's build and climb batch 20's fork 7.
- **`Condition`, 3:**
  - Its `extends` clause. The component's `Condition` extends `ZeroIndexed`, and the api puts `ZeroIndexed` on `Maybe` instead (fsi:913, :975; fss:1518).
  - Two result types, narrower in the component: `indexValuePairs` and `ivmap` answer `Condition[\…\]` where the api has `Generator[\…\]`.
  - And, accepted by the name gap: `indices`, wider in the component.

  Which of `Condition` and `Maybe` is `ZeroIndexed` in Part IV is a choice of the type hierarchy, beside `Maybe`'s own entries.

### 3.5 Waiting elsewhere, 18, listed and not fixed (the brief's item 4)

- **`Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing`, 5 (P-90):** `Maybe`'s extends clause; `Just`'s and `Nothing`'s subscripts at a `Range` against the component's at a `ZZ32`; `Just`'s `SQCAP` and `SQCUP`.
  - `AnyMaybe`'s `holds` is 4i's and `AnyUniqueItem`'s `holds` is 4h's. Neither waits.
  - Run S3: after 4h and 4i, all 5 remain.
- **`String`, 13 (P-155):**
  - By kind: 5 are 4h's (`size`, `asFlatString`, `uncheckedSubstring`, two `||`), 2 are 4i's (`splitWithOffsets`, `split`), 2 are header clauses (its excludes and extends) and 4 are api members that the component lacks (`depth`, `isBalanced`, `verify`, `rangeContains`). One more, `balanced`, is accepted by the name gap.
  - Run S3: after 4h and 4i, 11 remain, since the patch leaves `String` alone.

## 4. The 4h patch, measured

### 4.1 What it is

`library-4h.patch`: `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` alone, 65 insertions and 63 deletions. It holds 56 lines that take `abstract`, 3 added declarations, 6 changed lines and 1 removed line (section 3.1).

The first draft put `OpenRange`'s `abstract forward()` before its getters. The parser refuses that: 'Field/getter/setter declarations should come before method declarations.' (fsi:2218-2221 of the draft). In the patch it follows them. That draft's run is section 6, defect 4.

### 4.2 The sites, before and after

Command: `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/dist-4h/distance.txt tmp/dist-4h`, then `python3 -I explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/compare-sites.py explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv tmp/dist-4h/errors.tsv`. It prints:

    landled 5 now 28        (sic: 'landed 5 now 28')
    export 'are not matched by the declarations': landed 43 entries, now 20
      entry COME   (TraitDecl Array2 at FortressLibrary.fsi:L, due to different method bounds @ FortressLibrary.fsi:L)
      entry COME   (TraitDecl QQ at FortressLibrary.fsi:L, due to Asbtract method numerator @ FortressLibrary.fss:L is not declared in the API)

Site by site:

| Site | Class | Before (gate) | After 4h (run A) | After 4h and the follow-on (run B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FortressLibrary.fss:12`, export | X1 | 1 error, 43 entries | 1 error, 20 entries | 1 error, 20 entries |
| `FortressLibrary.fss:4386`, `BIG MIN` | BR | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `FortressLibrary.fss:4392`, `BIG MIN` | BR | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `FortressLibrary.fss:1465`, the fused arm | OT | 1 | 1 | 1 |

| **`#total`** | | **5** | **28** | **5** |

The two entries that come after 4h are the same traits that the message named before, narrowed: `Array2` now differs only in `bounds`, and `QQ` names `numerator` where it named `isNaN`. The 20 entries after 4h are:

- Nothing, Indexed, DelegatedIndexed, ReadableArray, ImmutableArray1, Array1, Array2, Array3;
- ActualReduction, BigReduction, Comprehension, Range, String, RR64, QQ;
- Equality, Condition, AnyMaybe, Maybe, Just.

The stage's own reading of run A: '#kind abstract-method 22', '#kind other/overloading 1', '#class D2 22', '#class OT 3'. `errors.py`'s pattern does not take the name `prefix BITNOT`, so one abstract-method error is counted as other (section 6, defect 5).

### 4.3 Each new error, the line that brings it, and the line that clears it

- **`BigNum`, 15** (`FortressBuiltin.fss:563`, `value object BigNum extends ZZ`): 'The inherited abstract method BITAND(self:(Integral[\I\] & {I}),b:I):I from the trait Integral[\ZZ\] has no concrete implementation in the object BigNum in component FortressBuiltin.' The others are the same for `BITOR`, `BITXOR`, `CHOOSE`, `DIV`, `GCD`, `LCM`, `LSHIFT`, `MOD`, `REM`, `RSHIFT`, `^`, `getter one`, `getter zero` and `prefix BITNOT`.
  - Each comes from the matching `abstract` line in `Integral` (fsi:448-473).
  - `ZZ`'s component defines all 15 (fss:990 on), and `ZZ`'s api shows none of them (fsi:646-679). `FortressBuiltin` sees `ZZ` through the api.
- **`Int` and `Long`, 1 each** (`FortressBuiltin.fss:367`, `:376`): `^(self, b:AnyIntegral)` from `Integral[\ZZ32\]` and `Integral[\ZZ64\]`. It comes from `Integral`'s `abstract opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):I` (fsi:473). `ZZ32`'s and `ZZ64`'s components define it, and their apis show only the `IntLiteral` form. `NN64`'s api shows both (fsi:525-526).
- **The open ranges, 6** (`RangeInternals.fss:349`, `:380`, `:398`): 'The inherited abstract method shiftLeft(amount:I):Range[\I\] from the trait Range[\ZZ32\] has no concrete implementation in the object OpenScalarRange in component RangeInternals.' The others are the same for `shiftRight`, and for `OpenRange2D` and `OpenRange3D`. They come from `Range`'s `abstract shiftLeft` and `abstract shiftRight` (fsi:2207-2208). `OpenRange`'s component defines both (`= self`, fss:4051-4052), and its api does not show them.

The follow-on, 19 api lines, each the component's own header of a member that it defines. Applied after the patch:

    trait ZZ32 ...          +    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):ZZ32           (before its IntLiteral form)
    trait ZZ64 ...          +    opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):ZZ64           (the same)
    trait ZZ ...            +    getter zero(): ZZ                          (after the coercions)
                            +    getter one(): ZZ
                            +    opr DIV(self, b: ZZ): ZZ                   (after opr /)
                            +    opr REM(self, b: ZZ): ZZ
                            +    opr MOD(self, b: ZZ): ZZ
                            +    opr GCD(self, b: ZZ): ZZ

    trait OpenRange[\I\]    +    shiftLeft(amount: I): OpenRange[\I\]       (after opr IN)
